To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dermal lesions of heat and electrical injuries are not specific, but that the changes in the cathodal area of electrical injury are specific from day 0-7, when the energy was delivered via a pointed electrode.
the changes in dermis are specific for electrically induced injuries and that the cathode lesions are specific for alternating current.

1) the histological changes in dermis are specific for electrically induced injuries; 2) the histological findings are not specific for the type of electric current used; 3) the histological appearance of dermis is not specific to the type of electrode used; 4) the histological appearances are specific to the location of the electrodes (anode and cathode).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the morphogenesis of electric and heat-induced changes in dermis.
the development of a method for differentiating between electrical and heat lesions.

the development of dermal changes in electrically and heat-injured skin in pigs, which may serve as a model for human skin, and with the establishment of criteria for differentiating between sequelae of electrically and of heat-induced dermal injuries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dermal changes in electrically induced lesions are specific for electrical energy from day 1 and up to 14 days after the injury, but only when the energy is transferred via a pointed electrode.
dermal changes specific to electrical injury could be found up to 7 days after the injury, but that the changes were more pronounced when using a pointed electrode and when applying direct current.

the changes in the anodally exposed dermis are non specific and that changes in cathodally exposed dermal tissue are specific for electrical injuries from day 1-14, when using 50 Hz a c. via a pointed electrode.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dermal lesions in the cathode areas are specific for electrical energy, while the dermal lesions of the anode areas and those of the 50 Hz alternating currents are non specific.

the dermal pathological evidence for distinguishing between sequel of electrical torture and that of other superficial injuries is present in the first week after injury, but the changes in collagen fibres may be present for several months after the injury.
the dermal lesions in the cathode areas are specific for electrical energy, while the lesions in the anode areas are non-specific and resemble heat lesions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the dermal lesions in the cathode areas of the 50-Hz a.c. lesions are specific for electrical injuries, but the changes are not specific enough to be used in the differentiation between 50-Hz and 60-Hz a.c., or to distinguish between a.c. and d.c. lesions.
the dermal lesions from heat injury can be differentiated from those of 50 Hz a c. and direct current.
the changes in the dermis are specific for electrical torture and can be used as pathological evidence for distinguishing it from heat lesions.
